examples.en: I have lived in Gangnam District since last year.
Where is Seocho District on the Seoul map?
This neighborhood is much quieter than Songpa District.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 저희 회사가 종로구로 이사해요.
examples.en: Next month our company is moving to Jongno District.

examples.ko: 우리 구에는 큰 공원이 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are two big parks in our district.

examples.ko: 서울에는 구가 모두 스물다섯 개 있어요.
examples.en: Seoul has twenty-five districts in total.

explain: 서울이나 부산 같은 큰 도시를 나눈 행정 구역이에요. '강남구', '마포구'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙이고, 구 안에는 다시 '동'이 있어요. 숫자 9를 읽는 '구'와 소리가 같아서 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.en: I'm going to the district office tomorrow to get a document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주민등록 같은 행정 일을 처리하러 동네 관청에 갈 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when going to the local district office to take care of administrative business.

explain_en: It is an administrative district of a big city such as Seoul or Busan. It goes after the name, as in 강남구 and 마포구, and a 구 is divided into smaller 동 areas. It sounds the same as the number 9 (구), so you tell them apart by context.

examples.en: I'm full today, so just water, please.
I exercise only on weekends.

examples.ko: 동생은 공부는 안 하고 게임만 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling doesn't study and only plays games.
Please explain it just one more time.
That shop closes only on Mondays.
I'll have just one cup of coffee today.

explain: '은/는, 이/가, 을/를' 자리에는 '물만 마셔요'처럼 '만'이 대신 오고, '집에서만, 친구에게만'처럼 다른 조사 뒤에도 붙어요. '밖에'는 꼭 부정과 함께 쓰지만 '만'은 긍정문에도 써요. 숫자 10000을 뜻하는 '만'과는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I'm busy now, so please wait just a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 시간만 기다려 달라고 부탁할 때 자주 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to ask someone to wait for only a short time.

explain_en: In subject or object position, '만' replaces the particle, as in '물만 마셔요', and it can also follow other particles, as in '집에서만' and '친구에게만'. Unlike '밖에', which needs a negative, '만' works in positive sentences too. It is a different word from '만' meaning ten thousand.

examples.en: This book is really interesting.
Excuse me, how much is this bag right now?
Is there a good restaurant near here?
I took this photo on Jeju Island.
I listen to this song every day.

examples.ko: 이 중에서 어떤 색을 제일 좋아해요?
examples.en: Which color do you like best among these?

explain: '이'는 말하는 사람 가까이에 있는 것, '그'는 듣는 사람 가까이나 이미 말한 것, '저'는 둘 다에게서 먼 것에 써요. 뒤에 꼭 명사가 와야 하고, 혼자 쓸 때는 '이것'이나 '이거'를 써요. 숫자 2, 이빨(tooth)의 '이'와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: This much is enough, so don't worry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 있는 양이나 수준을 가리키며 말할 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when pointing to the present amount or level of something.

explain_en: '이' points to what is near the speaker, '그' to what is near the listener or already mentioned, and '저' to what is far from both. A noun must follow it, and on its own you say '이것' or '이거'. It is a different word from '이' meaning two or tooth.

examples.en: This fabric is soft and pretty.
I bought fabric to make curtains.
The fabric is so thin that you can see through it.
I made a bag myself out of fabric.
This sofa is fabric, so it's hard to clean.

examples.ko: 그 가게에는 천 종류가 정말 많아요.
examples.en: That shop has a really wide variety of fabrics.

explain: 옷이나 커튼, 가방을 만드는 재료인 '천'이에요. 옷을 만들 재료는 '옷감'이라고도 하고, 작은 조각은 '헝겊'이라고 해요. 숫자 1000을 읽는 '천'과 소리가 같아서 '천을 사다'와 '천 원'처럼 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.example: 저는 장을 볼 때 천 가방을 써요.
phrases.en: I use a cloth bag when I go grocery shopping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천으로 만든 가방을 말할 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a bag made of fabric.

explain_en: It is the material used to make clothes, curtains and bags. The material for clothes is also called '옷감', and a small piece is a '헝겊'. It sounds the same as the number 1000 (천), so context such as '천을 사다' versus '천 원' tells them apart.
